payload.title: Execute ClayCode APP-06 staged bootstrap tool on Ubuntu

work_clay.goal: After the current strict parser/frontend closure is adequate, implement the smallest real Clay-authored parser/compiler/interpreter needed for APP-06, compile and execute it with the production ClayCode Stage1 compiler/runtime on Andreas' Ubuntu developer system, and measure semantic correctness, reproducibility and bootstrap lineage as separate receipt dimensions.
staging_candidate: Stage0: pinned host bootstrap toolchain/runtime with exact versions and hashes
Stage1: production ClayCode compiler/runtime built or packaged through the host toolchain
Stage1C: Clay-authored APP-06 microtool compiled and executed by Stage1
Stage2: partial/full ClayCode compiler self-host only after generic language/runtime closure
Stage3: same-source rebuild comparison under normalized build environment
Later hardening: diverse-backend/DDC-style verification where assumptions and cost justify it
hard_rules: Do not count full self-hosting as an unstated BASE requirement.
Do not change ClayCode semantics unless an executable application/compiler counterexample proves the existing semantic basis cannot express/lower the required program.
Do not collapse ProgramSemanticId, compiler/runtime identity, build-environment identity and output artifact hash into one identity.
Byte-identical rebuild is not by itself compiler semantic correctness or trusting-trust closure.
Target-host execution receipts are required for BASE application acceptance.

reason_clay.why_now: BASE_CLAYCODE_RELEASE remains NOT_PASS. APP-06 Compiler/Tool, compiler/lowering, fuzz/conformance and BASE audit are open. Recent work also preserves a strict LALR negative, so the bootstrap tool must not bypass frontend closure.

required_outputs: exact Stage0 host compiler/runtime/parser/toolchain versions and hashes
Stage1 ClayCode compiler/runtime identity and build receipt
Clay-authored APP-06 microtool source/IR semantic hash
successful Stage1 compile/lower and actual APP-06 execution receipt
deterministic positive/negative semantic corpus with expected-vs-observed results
build-variation matrix covering at least build path plus any observable timestamp/order/environment dimensions relevant to generated artifacts
normalization mechanisms and explicit build-environment contract
separate semantic-equivalence, byte-reproducibility and compiler-diversity receipt fields
decision whether Stage2/Stage3 self-host is ready or remains deferred
all negative results and unresolved language counterexamples preserved
completion_clay.pass_condition: APP-06 microtool is genuinely authored using admitted ClayCode facilities, compiled/lowered by the production compiler/runtime, executed on the target Ubuntu host with positive and negative tests, and leaves exact semantic/build/artifact provenance. Full self-host is not required for this work item's APP-06 completion unless the current acceptance contract is explicitly strengthened.

executor_policy.reason: The exact target-host compiler/runtime and Ubuntu build environment are only established by verified local execution.

dependencies: Current strict parser conflict/front-end closure must be resolved or an explicitly selected deterministic parser strategy must exist.
Generic typed function/control/data/error facilities needed by the chosen APP-06 microtool must be admitted and executable.
Production Stage1 ClayCode compiler/runtime path must exist far enough to compile the microtool.
Latest work specification must be revalidated immediately before effect.
invalidators: An equal-or-stronger target-host APP-06 bootstrap/self-host receipt already completes the same discriminators.
The owner explicitly strengthens or changes the BASE acceptance contract to require full self-hosting.
A newer executable compiler counterexample changes the required staging sequence.
